source.title: Why Does Adaptive Batching Help LLM Pretraining? A Perspective from Unbounded Variance
source.authors: Arda Fazla; Antesh Upadhyay; Ege C. Kaya; M. Şahin; Abolfazl Hashemi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and tables.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares fixed small and large batches and an adaptive schedule, and its results qualify the batch-size/generalization relationship across online pretraining and multi-epoch image classification.
record.gate_note: The study measures gradient-noise growth at perturbed parameters, but that is not a result on a mapped claim version. Rows below record reported validation, training, and test losses for the batch-size comparisons; cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Fixed-batch comparisons measure held-out loss under equal training exposure and bear on V5. CIFAR shows a large-batch penalty; ImageNet and larger online language models qualify its scope under learning-rate scaling and warmup. Matched token budgets control sample exposure in single-pass pretraining, although this differs from multi-epoch training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors explain adaptive batching through displacement-dependent gradient noise and report lower validation loss than both fixed batches in online OLMo2 pretraining. In multi-epoch vision training, BG-a lowers training loss relative to small batches, while small batches retain the lowest test loss on CIFAR. ImageNet is an exception: fixed large batches have the lowest test loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces a displacement-dependent adaptive batch scheduler and compares it with fixed batches. It scales learning rates with batch size; LLM runs use AdamW and matched token budgets, while vision runs use momentum SGD and matched epochs.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by dataset and training regime: small batch has the best test loss on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; large batch has the best test loss on ImageNet-1K. Among OLMo2 models, the fixed large batch is worse than small at 100M but better at 600M and 1B.

fits_no_version.finding: Stochastic-gradient variance grows subquadratically with displacement from initialization at randomly perturbed parameter states.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-noise growth can be modeled using a displacement-dependent exponent; this does not establish magnitude-aware sharpness tracking generalization gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: Large or adaptive batches often lower training loss relative to small batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch-size recipes affect optimization under equal sample budgets; training loss alone does not establish held-out generalization.

record.problems: Preprint. LLM experiments cover OLMo2 up to 1B parameters on C4; authors note that larger scales and other corpora remain unevaluated. Vision comparisons are on three datasets with ResNet50. Adaptive and large-batch learning rates are scaled from the small-batch tuned learning rate without additional tuning.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The reported gradient-noise fits and downstream benchmark accuracies were not extracted because they do not directly measure a mapped version's batch-size/generalization relationship.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in the same architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Within-workload adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons; optimizer choice is confounded with workload here.

Longer-training remedies, isolated effects of scaling or warmup, normalization and regularization changes, and multi-epoch language-model training. Only two fixed batch sizes per workload are compared, so critical batch thresholds are not identified.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap rankings. Gradient-noise variance at perturbed initialization is a different measure.

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Reported uncertainties are standard deviations over three seeds, not significance tests. Large-batch and BG-a learning rates are scaled from the small-batch tuned rate without separate tuning. Reversed results under scaling and warmup qualify V5 rather than contradict its explicit adapted-recipe exceptions. Downstream accuracies are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization comparisons.
Language-model fixed-epoch comparisons; the LLM runs use matched token budgets. The paper tests its own adaptive scheduler, not all listed adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
